pathway.title: Elanco Animal Health Inc — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, liquidity and the near maturity profile are strong relative to obligations. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated held cash of USD 530 million and about USD 915 million of undrawn facilities at 2026-06-30, a total of USD 1,445 million, which is 11.5 times the USD 126 million of required principal payments in 2026 and 2027 [CP-1]. No facility matures before June 2028, so liquidity is not a near-term constraint on this evidence.

Second, leverage has improved but its level depends on the definition. Total debt including the finance lease fell from 4.49x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at 2025-12-31 to 3.91x at 2026-06-30 and net leverage on the company's definition fell from 3.6x to 3.1x [CP-1]. Most of the improvement came from higher Adjusted EBITDA rather than repayment: debt fell by USD 101 million while trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 901 million to USD 1,008 million [CP-1]. On reported EBITDA the same total debt is 5.10x.

Third, the quality of Adjusted EBITDA is the main analytical risk. Net add-backs of USD 236 million equal 31 percent of reported trailing EBITDA of USD 773 million, special charges have run at USD 127 million, USD 150 million, USD 237 million and USD 252 million in FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and the trailing twelve months, and part of the restructuring is cash with a reserve of USD 86 million still to be paid [CP-1]. The removal of sold royalty revenue works in the other direction and makes the measure more conservative on that item [CP-1].

Fourth, important claims sit outside the leverage ratio. The liability for sale of future revenue to Blackstone is USD 315 million with an effective interest rate of 18.3 percent, the headquarters finance lease has a USD 250 million purchase option or landlord put in 2030 that management expects to exercise, the AHV acquisition carries USD 100 million of deferred cash and up to USD 140 million of contingent payments, and pension funded status is USD (150) million [CP-1; CP-1A]. The pack does not show how these rank against lenders or whether the royalty rights were collateral.

Fifth, 2028 is the refinancing event. USD 1,236 million of required principal falls due in 2028, which is 33 percent of the scheduled total and includes the USD 750 million senior notes due 2028-08-28, an incremental term facility due 2028-08-12 and the securitization facility due June 2028 [CP-1]. The company refinanced its 2027 term loan in October 2025 into facilities maturing in 2029 and 2032, which shows market access, and management targets net leverage below 3x in 2027 [CP-1A].

Sixth, interest sensitivity is rising. Interest rate swaps of USD 2,300 million notional mature in August 2026 against forward-starting swaps of USD 1,450 million, so unhedged floating-rate debt rises from USD 639 million to USD 1,489 million on the pack's figures, about USD 15 million a year for each 100 basis points before any later hedging that the pack does not show [CP-1]. Fiscal year 2025 cash interest cover on Adjusted EBITDA was 4.37x, or 3.62x before interest received on net investment hedges [CP-1]; trailing cash interest is not supplied.

Seventh, the information base limits confidence. Covenant levels are printed but achieved ratios are not, the credit agreement, indenture, guarantor list and collateral are not supplied, there are no ratings, and nothing after 2026-08-05 is in the pack [CP-0; CP-1]. On the proxies in the financial base, trailing Adjusted EBITDA could fall by about 59 percent before the leverage covenant level is reached and by about 54 percent before the interest cover level is reached, but covenant definitions differ and these are not headroom.

runs.text: Strengths. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated has a diversified revenue base across pet health and farm animal products, about 200 brands and more than 90 countries, with Q2 2026 revenue up 10 percent reported and 8 percent in organic constant currency, driven by new products [CP-1; CP-1A]. Liquidity of USD 1,445 million and a light maturity schedule before 2028 provide time. Gross margin rose to 58.3 percent in Q2 2026 from 57.5 percent, and operating cash flow was USD 290 million in six months 2026 against USD 233 million, with net capital spending falling to USD 84 million from USD 122 million, so operating cash flow less net purchases was USD 379 million trailing [CP-1]. There is no sponsor, no dividend and no buyback beyond employee tax withholding, and the company repaid a net USD 563 million of borrowings in 2025 [CP-1A]. The October 2025 refinancing extended maturities. Covenant levels of 7.71 to 1.00 and 2.00 to 1.00 sit far from the proxies computed from the pack [CP-1].

Weaknesses. Leverage remains high at 3.91x on total debt and 5.10x on reported EBITDA, the trailing reported result is a loss of USD 199 million, and tangible equity is negative at USD (1,461) million because goodwill and intangibles exceed total equity [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA relies on add-backs of USD 236 million, including cash restructuring. Claims outside the debt table, hedge roll-off, customer concentration (two distributors at about 19 percent of FY2025 revenue) and product concentration (five families at about 38 percent) add cash flow volatility, and the first half carries most of the parasiticide sales [CP-1; CP-1A]. The senior notes coupon of 4.900 percent has reset to 6.40 percent after earlier downgrades, which shows the cost of credit events [CP-1]. Governance documents, guarantor and collateral structure, achieved covenant ratios and ratings are missing, and the stated capital allocation flexibility at below 3x leverage is a monitoring point [CP-1A].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No new debt issue, sponsor transaction or change of control appears in the evidence after 2025-12-31. The relevant transactions are as follows. On 2025-10-31 Elanco refinanced the Term Loan B due 2027, paying off a balance of 2,102, with three new facilities of aggregate gross proceeds of 2,106 (the Term Loan B due 2032 of 1,100, the Euro Term Loan due 2029 of 400 million euros and the Incremental Term Facility due 2032 of 540) plus cash on hand; issuance costs and discounts were about 32 and 20 was charged to interest expense for refinancing costs and deferred cost write-offs (10-K page:75, page:109). The documented purpose was to extend the debt maturity profile and lower cash interest, which is a supportive action for creditors. In May 2025 Elanco sold to Blackstone the rights to U.S. royalties and sales milestones on XDEMVY owed by Tarsus for 295, with net proceeds of 290 used to repay debt; the rights run for U.S. net sales from 2025-04-01 to 2033-08-24, Elanco keeps ex-U.S. royalties and later U.S. royalties, and the liability is carried at 315 at 2026-06-30 with an effective interest rate of 18.3 percent (10-K page:75-76; Q2 10-Q page:17). That cost of capital is high against the term loans priced at Term SOFR plus 1.75 to 2.25 percent, and the pack does not say whether the royalty rights were part of the lenders' collateral. In June 2025 Elanco started a five-year finance lease on its new Indianapolis headquarters, with a purchase option and a landlord put at 250 at the end of the term, which management expects to exercise (10-K page:76, page:121); a City of Indianapolis tax increment incentive totalling 64 funds part of the project (page:121). In June 2025 the securitization facility was amended to extend its maturity to June 2028 (page:111). On 2026-02-19 Elanco signed to buy AHV International B.V., a Netherlands farm animal health company (10-K page:138, a subsequent event to that report), and closed on 2026-04-30 for total estimated purchase consideration of 243: 76 cash paid at closing, 100 of deferred cash due through 2030 and a contingent consideration fair value of 67 for up to 140 of milestone payments through 2032 (Q2 10-Q page:10). The acquisition was funded from cash on hand and a 50 draw on the securitization facility, drawn on 2026-04-22 and repaid in the quarter (Q1 10-Q page:11; Q2 10-Q page:30). Management says the deal does not materially affect the deleveraging timeline (Q2 10-Q page:30), a management statement. In 2024 Elanco sold its aqua business to Merck Animal Health for 1,294 in cash, used mostly to repay term loan debt (10-K page:105). Financing documents for these transactions are not in the pack and are known only through the descriptions cited. The Q4 2025 rating upgrade is described only through the senior notes rate reset from 6.650 to 6.40 percent (10-K page:111; Q2 10-Q page:12).

fields.value: Question for this module: build the financial base for the credit snapshot from the pinned filings and releases. That means reported statements, discrete and trailing periods, the Adjusted EBITDA bridge, debt and maturity structure, liquidity, cash flow quality, interest and leverage ratios, and the covenant picture, each labelled by period and perimeter. It uses the readiness handoff (CP-0) and carries its limitations. Locator abbreviations: 10-K is the FY2025 annual report; Q3-25 10-Q, Q1 10-Q and Q2 10-Q are the quarterly reports for the quarters ended 2025-09-30, 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30; Feb release, May release and Aug release are the earnings release exhibits dated 2026-02-24, 2026-05-06 and 2026-08-05. `page:N` is the extraction chunk, not the printed page. The context holds no ratings, quotes, deal terms or assumptions; blanks are not zero.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot, with the limits stated below. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated reports one consolidated perimeter and one segment, so every figure is group level. Revenue was 4,715 in FY2025 and 2,739 in the six months to 2026-06-30, up from 2,434 a year earlier; the trailing twelve month figure is 5,020. Reported net income was a loss of 232 in FY2025 because the fourth quarter carried 202 of impairment and restructuring charges; the trailing twelve month reported result is still a loss of 199, while six-month 2026 net income is 111. Adjusted EBITDA, which management defines and the filed statements do not print, was 901 in FY2025 and is printed as 1,008 for the trailing twelve months at 2026-06-30 (1,009 when rebuilt from the components, a rounding difference). Reported EBITDA from the same reconciliation is 773 on a trailing basis, so the net add-backs are 236.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage depends on the definition. Management's net leverage, which deducts cash and the finance lease from gross debt, is 3.6x at 2025-12-31 and 3.1x at 2026-06-30. On a basis that keeps the 255 headquarters finance lease in debt and deducts only cash, net debt is 3,414 and net leverage 3.39x at 2026-06-30, and total debt leverage is 3.91x. On reported EBITDA, which still includes royalty revenue that is no longer received in cash, total debt leverage is 5.10x. Both bases are shown in the charts and the table because the choice moves the answer by nearly two turns between the lowest basis (3.13x, the company's) and the highest (5.10x, reported EBITDA).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt is bank term loans, a securitization facility and 750 of senior notes due 2028. Required principal payments are small until 2028, when 1,236 falls due, and 1,860 falls due in 2031 and later. Liquidity at 2026-06-30 is 530 of cash plus about 750 of undrawn revolver and about 165 of undrawn securitization capacity, 1,445 in total, and no facility matures before June 2028, when the securitization facility falls due. Operating cash flow was 290 in the six months, and operating cash flow less net purchases of property, equipment and software was 206. The main watch items are the dependence of Adjusted EBITDA on add-backs that include cash restructuring, the August 2026 roll-off of 2,300 of interest rate swaps, the debt-like claims outside the debt table (the 315 liability for sale of future revenue, the headquarters lease purchase option and acquisition payments) and the absence of any figure after 2026-08-05. Adjusted EBITDA, net leverage and guidance are management claims; the filed statements control every other figure.

fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA starts from reported net income, adds net interest expense, income tax and depreciation and amortization to reach EBITDA, then adjusts for the cost of sales items, asset impairment, restructuring and other special charges, sold royalty revenue, the 2024 divestiture gain and other (income) expense items (Aug release page:14; Feb release page:18). For the trailing twelve months the adjustments are 252 of impairment, restructuring and other special charges, less 33 of sold royalty revenue, plus 16 of other expense items and 1 of cost of sales, in total 236, equal to 31 percent of reported EBITDA of 773 (calculation below). Three points matter for credit use. First, the sold royalty adjustment removes revenue that Elanco still books under GAAP but no longer receives in cash, because the XDEMVY royalties go to Blackstone through 2033-08-24 (Q2 10-Q page:17); removing it makes Adjusted EBITDA the more conservative measure on that item. Second, the special charges are not one-off in size or frequency: they were 127 in FY2023, 150 in FY2024, 237 in FY2025 and 252 trailing (10-K page:92; Q2 10-Q page:6). Third, the FY2025 charges include 155 of restructuring of which 116 is cash severance (Feb release page:3, page:5); the restructuring reserve stood at 124 at 2025-12-31 and 86 at 2026-06-30, with about 80 classified as current (Q2 10-Q page:11-12). That cash is spent after the add-back and does not appear in Adjusted EBITDA, though it is in operating cash flow.

fields.value: At 2026-06-30 floating-rate borrowings are the six term facilities (2,839) plus the securitization facility (100), 2,939 in total, against 750 of fixed-rate notes. Interest rate swaps of 2,300 notional convert floating to fixed and have scheduled maturities in August 2026; forward-starting swaps of 1,450 notional become effective in August 2026 with maturities between 2027 and 2031, up from 850 at 2025-12-31 (Q2 10-Q page:14). On the pack's figures the hedged floating debt falls from 2,300 to 1,450 after August 2026 and unhedged floating-rate borrowings rise from 639 to 1,489, before any hedging added after 2026-06-30, which the pack does not show. The company states that approximately 80 percent of borrowings were fixed or swapped at 2026-06-30 (page:12). The calculation below gives about 83 percent for the pre-August position and about 60 percent for the post-August position on the same base; the post-August figure is an analyst illustration, not a company statement. Net investment hedges (1,000 million CHF notional with tenors in 2026 and 2027, of which 200 million CHF was extended to 2031 in July 2026) generated 23 of interest income in six months 2026, recorded as a reduction of interest expense (page:13-14).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two financial maintenance covenants apply under the Revolving Credit Facility and, on consistent terms, the Euro Term Loan: a net total leverage ratio of pro forma net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA not to exceed 7.71 to 1.00 for the preceding four quarters, not subject to step-downs, and an interest coverage ratio of pro forma adjusted EBITDA to cash interest expense of no less than 2.00 to 1.00 (10-K page:109-110; Q3-25 10-Q page:15). The company states compliance with all covenants at 2026-06-30 (Q2 10-Q page:12). The achieved ratios are not supplied. Both covenant definitions differ from the metrics here: they use pro forma figures and covenant adjustments that the company says reduce its net leverage ratio below the printed measure (Aug release page:14), and a different net debt and cash interest definition. As an illustration only, not a covenant calculation: net debt of 3,159 divided by 7.71 is about 410, so trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 1,008 could fall by about 59 percent before the leverage test is reached on those proxies; and twice FY2025 cash interest of 206 is 412, so Adjusted EBITDA of 901 could fall by about 54 percent before the cover test is reached. The Senior Notes indenture has no financial maintenance covenant in the pack; it limits liens and sale-leasebacks and restricts mergers and sales of substantially all assets (10-K page:111). The Securitization Facility has covenants on the composition of the receivables portfolio, with compliance stated at 2025-12-31 (page:111).

fields.value: At 2026-06-30: cash and cash equivalents 530; revolver commitment 750, nothing drawn, unused capacity approximately 750; securitization facility drawn 100 with approximately 165 of undrawn capacity under a borrowing base (Q2 10-Q page:12, page:36). Total of these inputs is 1,445. No letters of credit or other usage of the revolver is printed in any source. The revolver matures in July 2029 and the securitization facility in June 2028, so no facility expires within twelve months of 2026-06-30. Known cash calls over the next twelve months that the pack supports: required amortization (63 for calendar 2026 and 63 for 2027 on the 2025-12-31 schedule), deferred AHV cash consideration of about 60 in January 2027, restructuring reserve payments (about 80 current), 2026 capital expenditure guided at 175 to 200 (10-K page:86), and interest. A fall in cash from 545 to 530 in six months came with 76 paid for the AHV acquisition, 89 of debt repayment and 35 of share withholding payments, against operating cash flow of 290.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was 560 in FY2025 and 290 in six months 2026 against 233 a year earlier. Quarterly operating cash flow was 13 in Q1 2026 and 277 in Q2 2026 (May release page:4; Aug release page:4), which shows the first-half seasonal pattern; the company notes that parasiticide sales concentrate in the first half (Q2 10-Q page:30). Working capital absorbed 239 in six months 2026 against 185, with receivables up from 873 to 1,077 and inventories up from 1,737 to 1,769 since 2025-12-31 (page:6-7). Net purchases of property, equipment and software fell to 84 from 122 on timing of the Elwood, Kansas monoclonal antibody plant spend (page:37). Cash taxes of 225 in FY2025 compare with a tax expense of 8, driven by payments on the 2024 aqua divestiture gain (10-K page:84, page:126-127), so FY2025 free cash flow is a poor guide to a normal tax year; six-month 2026 cash taxes are not supplied. Interest on the liability for sale of future revenue and the sold royalties are non-cash and sit in operating cash flow adjustments (Q2 10-Q page:7).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Q2 2026 revenue was 1,368, up 10 percent reported and 8 percent in organic constant currency, with Pet Health 718 and Farm Animal 633 (Q2 10-Q page:9; Aug release page:2). Gross margin was 58.3 percent against 57.5 percent (page:32). Net income was 54 and Adjusted EBITDA 288. The AHV International acquisition closed 2026-04-30 for total estimated consideration of 243, with 76 paid in cash and funded from cash on hand and a 50 draw on the securitization facility, repaid in the quarter (page:10, page:30). Net leverage as reported fell from 3.5x to 3.1x in the quarter (May release page:4; Aug release page:4). Management raised 2026 guidance to revenue of 5,090 to 5,140 and Adjusted EBITDA of 1,010 to 1,035 and targeted year-end net leverage of approximately 3.0x (Aug release page:1, page:4); these are management claims. Subsequent items in the 10-Q are the July 2026 extension of 200 million CHF of net investment hedges to 2031 (page:13) and legal: the Ninth Circuit affirmed the Tevra verdict on 2026-07-06 and denied rehearing on 2026-07-31 (page:22). fields.value: Question for this module: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor, and what is the credit-relevant history? It builds the business and transaction fact pack, with governance and issuer behaviour judged only from documented actions. It uses the readiness handoff (CP-0) and the financial base (CP-1). It gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion. Row categories used below are Documentary Fact (the cited source states it), Management Language (management's characterisation, attributed), Analyst Interpretation (reading of cited evidence) and Insufficient Information (the datapoint is missing). Locator abbreviations: 10-K is the FY2025 annual report; Q1 10-Q and Q2 10-Q are the quarterly reports for the quarters ended 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30; Feb release, May release and Aug release are the earnings release exhibits dated 2026-02-24, 2026-05-06 and 2026-08-05. `page:N` is the extraction chunk, not the printed page. The context holds no sponsor, borrower, parent, guarantor, deal terms or research questions; those blanks are not zero. Sector and country in the context ("Pharmaceutical Preparations", "United States") are context labels, not issuer evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Elanco Animal Health Incorporated is a global animal health company selling pet health and farm animal products in more than 90 countries, with about 200 brands, as one reporting segment (10-K page:7-8; Q2 10-Q page:24, page:26). It was a Lilly business unit, became an independent company on 2018-09-18, completed separation from Lilly in March 2019 and bought Bayer Animal Health in August 2020 (10-K page:7). No sponsor, parent or controlling shareholder is evidenced in the pack, and the company says it does not anticipate paying dividends (10-K page:70). The creditor-relevant facts fall into three groups. First, the operating model is diversified by species and region but concentrated by channel and product: the largest customer was about 12 percent of FY2025 revenue and the top five product families about 38 percent, with seasonality in pet parasiticides that places most of Seresto and Advantage Family sales in the first half (10-K page:9, page:12-13). Second, the 2025 and 2026 transactions changed the capital structure: the October 2025 refinancing, the Blackstone sale of future royalties, the headquarters finance lease with a purchase option, and the AHV acquisition with deferred and contingent consideration. These are described in the Transaction summary and are priced in CP-1. Third, management is pursuing an innovation-led growth plan (Zenrelia, Credelio Quattro, Befrena) with a restructuring and a stated deleveraging path; those are management statements, and CP-1 shows that part of the improvement in leverage to date came from higher trailing Adjusted EBITDA rather than from repayment. Documented issuer behaviour is mainly supportive of creditors (debt repaid, no dividends, the AHV acquisition funded from cash on hand and a short-lived securitization draw), with two items that need monitoring: the use of a royalty monetization and a headquarters lease with a purchase option rather than debt, and management's statement that falling below 3x leverage will unlock capital allocation flexibility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt issue, sponsor transaction or change of control appears in the evidence after 2025-12-31. The relevant transactions are as follows. On 2025-10-31 Elanco refinanced the Term Loan B due 2027, paying off a balance of 2,102, with three new facilities of aggregate gross proceeds of 2,106 (the Term Loan B due 2032 of 1,100, the Euro Term Loan due 2029 of 400 million euros and the Incremental Term Facility due 2032 of 540) plus cash on hand; issuance costs and discounts were about 32 and 20 was charged to interest expense for refinancing costs and deferred cost write-offs (10-K page:75, page:109). The documented purpose was to extend the debt maturity profile and lower cash interest, which is a supportive action for creditors. In May 2025 Elanco sold to Blackstone the rights to U.S. royalties and sales milestones on XDEMVY owed by Tarsus for 295, with net proceeds of 290 used to repay debt; the rights run for U.S. net sales from 2025-04-01 to 2033-08-24, Elanco keeps ex-U.S. royalties and later U.S. royalties, and the liability is carried at 315 at 2026-06-30 with an effective interest rate of 18.3 percent (10-K page:75-76; Q2 10-Q page:17). That cost of capital is high against the term loans priced at Term SOFR plus 1.75 to 2.25 percent, and the pack does not say whether the royalty rights were part of the lenders' collateral. In June 2025 Elanco started a five-year finance lease on its new Indianapolis headquarters, with a purchase option and a landlord put at 250 at the end of the term, which management expects to exercise (10-K page:76, page:121); a City of Indianapolis tax increment incentive totalling 64 funds part of the project (page:121). In June 2025 the securitization facility was amended to extend its maturity to June 2028 (page:111). On 2026-02-19 Elanco signed to buy AHV International B.V., a Netherlands farm animal health company (10-K page:138, a subsequent event to that report), and closed on 2026-04-30 for total estimated purchase consideration of 243: 76 cash paid at closing, 100 of deferred cash due through 2030 and a contingent consideration fair value of 67 for up to 140 of milestone payments through 2032 (Q2 10-Q page:10). The acquisition was funded from cash on hand and a 50 draw on the securitization facility, drawn on 2026-04-22 and repaid in the quarter (Q1 10-Q page:11; Q2 10-Q page:30). Management says the deal does not materially affect the deleveraging timeline (Q2 10-Q page:30), a management statement. In 2024 Elanco sold its aqua business to Merck Animal Health for 1,294 in cash, used mostly to repay term loan debt (10-K page:105). Financing documents for these transactions are not in the pack and are known only through the descriptions cited. The Q4 2025 rating upgrade is described only through the senior notes rate reset from 6.650 to 6.40 percent (10-K page:111; Q2 10-Q page:12).

fields.value: Revenue durability. Evidence: Pet Health volume growth in Q2 2026 was driven by new products Zenrelia and Credelio Quattro, and the largest customer is a distributor about 12 percent of FY2025 revenue (Q2 10-Q page:32; 10-K page:13). Risk mechanic: new-product volume supports revenue growth now, but a small number of distributors and five product families carry the base, so a destocking or competitive event transmits quickly to revenue and receivables. Credit implication: revenue visibility is good in the near term and concentrated in the medium term; monitor distributor inventory and new product share.

fields.value: Cash conversion and add-backs. Evidence: CP-1 shows trailing net add-backs of 236 to reported EBITDA, partly cash restructuring, and a restructuring reserve of 86 (Q2 10-Q page:11-12). Risk mechanic: cash costs paid after the add-back reduce cash available for debt service. Credit implication: leverage on Adjusted EBITDA overstates cash capacity until the reserve is paid; test free cash flow alongside the measure. The conflict logged below on AHV payments does not counter this.

Risk mechanic: these claim cash flow through 2033 without appearing in the leverage ratio. Credit implication: debt service coverage should include them; the pack does not show their ranking against lenders.

Evidence: no sponsor, no dividends and an explicit statement that capital allocation flexibility follows leverage below 3x (10-K page:70; Aug release page:4). Risk mechanic: absence of a sponsor removes sponsor-extraction risk, but the stated flexibility could be used for distributions or acquisitions funded by new debt. Credit implication: monitoring posture should watch restricted payment and acquisition activity once leverage approaches the target.

fields.value: This is the fundamental credit synthesis for Elanco Animal Health Inc as of 2026-11-05 on the credit_snapshot pathway. It synthesises the readiness (CP-0), financial base (CP-1) and business and transaction (CP-1A) handoffs, with spot checks against the pinned filings, and carries their limits. It gives no ratings, relative value, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Evidence is the upstream handoffs. The pinned sources were opened to spot check the figures this module repeats; each is listed with the use made of it. Locator abbreviations: 10-K is the FY2025 annual report; Q2 10-Q is the report for the quarter ended 2026-06-30; Aug release is the earnings release dated 2026-08-05. `page:N` is the extraction chunk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Elanco Animal Health Incorporated is a moderately leveraged but improving credit whose liquidity and maturity profile are adequate and whose main weakness is the quality and definition of its leverage. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,445 million at 2026-06-30 and required principal payments of only USD 63 million in each of 2026 and 2027, with no large maturity before 2028. The weakest point is that total debt including the finance lease is 3.91x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, against management's 3.1x net measure, while Adjusted EBITDA includes net add-backs of USD 236 million and claims outside the debt table sit beside it. What decides the outcome is whether trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,008 million converts to cash after restructuring, interest and a rising floating-rate exposure, and whether the USD 1,236 million falling due in 2028 is refinanced on similar terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, liquidity and the near maturity profile are strong relative to obligations. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated held cash of USD 530 million and about USD 915 million of undrawn facilities at 2026-06-30, a total of USD 1,445 million, which is 11.5 times the USD 126 million of required principal payments in 2026 and 2027 [CP-1]. No facility matures before June 2028, so liquidity is not a near-term constraint on this evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, leverage has improved but its level depends on the definition. Total debt including the finance lease fell from 4.49x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at 2025-12-31 to 3.91x at 2026-06-30 and net leverage on the company's definition fell from 3.6x to 3.1x [CP-1]. Most of the improvement came from higher Adjusted EBITDA rather than repayment: debt fell by USD 101 million while trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 901 million to USD 1,008 million [CP-1]. On reported EBITDA the same total debt is 5.10x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, the quality of Adjusted EBITDA is the main analytical risk. Net add-backs of USD 236 million equal 31 percent of reported trailing EBITDA of USD 773 million, special charges have run at USD 127 million, USD 150 million, USD 237 million and USD 252 million in FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and the trailing twelve months, and part of the restructuring is cash with a reserve of USD 86 million still to be paid [CP-1]. The removal of sold royalty revenue works in the other direction and makes the measure more conservative on that item [CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, important claims sit outside the leverage ratio. The liability for sale of future revenue to Blackstone is USD 315 million with an effective interest rate of 18.3 percent, the headquarters finance lease has a USD 250 million purchase option or landlord put in 2030 that management expects to exercise, the AHV acquisition carries USD 100 million of deferred cash and up to USD 140 million of contingent payments, and pension funded status is USD (150) million [CP-1; CP-1A]. The pack does not show how these rank against lenders or whether the royalty rights were collateral.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, 2028 is the refinancing event. USD 1,236 million of required principal falls due in 2028, which is 33 percent of the scheduled total and includes the USD 750 million senior notes due 2028-08-28, an incremental term facility due 2028-08-12 and the securitization facility due June 2028 [CP-1]. The company refinanced its 2027 term loan in October 2025 into facilities maturing in 2029 and 2032, which shows market access, and management targets net leverage below 3x in 2027 [CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, interest sensitivity is rising. Interest rate swaps of USD 2,300 million notional mature in August 2026 against forward-starting swaps of USD 1,450 million, so unhedged floating-rate debt rises from USD 639 million to USD 1,489 million on the pack's figures, about USD 15 million a year for each 100 basis points before any later hedging that the pack does not show [CP-1]. Fiscal year 2025 cash interest cover on Adjusted EBITDA was 4.37x, or 3.62x before interest received on net investment hedges [CP-1]; trailing cash interest is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seventh, the information base limits confidence. Covenant levels are printed but achieved ratios are not, the credit agreement, indenture, guarantor list and collateral are not supplied, there are no ratings, and nothing after 2026-08-05 is in the pack [CP-0; CP-1]. On the proxies in the financial base, trailing Adjusted EBITDA could fall by about 59 percent before the leverage covenant level is reached and by about 54 percent before the interest cover level is reached, but covenant definitions differ and these are not headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Elanco Animal Health Incorporated has a diversified revenue base across pet health and farm animal products, about 200 brands and more than 90 countries, with Q2 2026 revenue up 10 percent reported and 8 percent in organic constant currency, driven by new products [CP-1; CP-1A]. Liquidity of USD 1,445 million and a light maturity schedule before 2028 provide time. Gross margin rose to 58.3 percent in Q2 2026 from 57.5 percent, and operating cash flow was USD 290 million in six months 2026 against USD 233 million, with net capital spending falling to USD 84 million from USD 122 million, so operating cash flow less net purchases was USD 379 million trailing [CP-1]. There is no sponsor, no dividend and no buyback beyond employee tax withholding, and the company repaid a net USD 563 million of borrowings in 2025 [CP-1A]. The October 2025 refinancing extended maturities. Covenant levels of 7.71 to 1.00 and 2.00 to 1.00 sit far from the proxies computed from the pack [CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage remains high at 3.91x on total debt and 5.10x on reported EBITDA, the trailing reported result is a loss of USD 199 million, and tangible equity is negative at USD (1,461) million because goodwill and intangibles exceed total equity [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA relies on add-backs of USD 236 million, including cash restructuring. Claims outside the debt table, hedge roll-off, customer concentration (two distributors at about 19 percent of FY2025 revenue) and product concentration (five families at about 38 percent) add cash flow volatility, and the first half carries most of the parasiticide sales [CP-1; CP-1A]. The senior notes coupon of 4.900 percent has reset to 6.40 percent after earlier downgrades, which shows the cost of credit events [CP-1]. Governance documents, guarantor and collateral structure, achieved covenant ratios and ratings are missing, and the stated capital allocation flexibility at below 3x leverage is a monitoring point [CP-1A].

fields.value: The strongest evidence against the cautious view is that Elanco generated operating cash flow of 290 in six months 2026 against 233, cut net capital spending to 84 from 122, took total debt including the lease from 4,045 to 3,944, holds 1,445 of liquidity, and has no facility maturing before June 2028. If trailing Adjusted EBITDA converts to cash as the first half suggests, deleveraging toward the management target of below 3x could come faster than the cautious view assumes. What would make that case win: third-quarter results with Adjusted EBITDA inside the 200 to 215 guided range, restructuring cash costs within the reserve of 86, and a refinancing of the 2028 maturities ahead of the August 2028 notes date. Downside chain with observable triggers: a distributor destocking or loss of Zenrelia share (first break: Pet Health volume, 718 in Q2) lowers Adjusted EBITDA; restructuring and acquisition payments continue regardless (transmission), drawing on cash of 530 and the undrawn revolver of about 750; unhedged floating-rate exposure of 1,489 raises interest; leverage drifts above 3.5x on the management measure ahead of the 1,236 due in 2028. Triggers to watch: quarterly Adjusted EBITDA against guidance, net leverage on the management measure, the revolver balance, any covenant certificate when obtainable, and hedge disclosures after August 2026.
